`??` gives a fallback for when the left side is `null` or `undefined`. A `!` on that side says it never is. If that is true, the fallback is dead code. If it is not, the `!` is wrong. `??` handles both cases without it, so remove the `!`.

A `!` on the right side is allowed.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
declare const settings: { theme?: string };
declare function findUser(id: string): { name: string } | null;

const theme = settings.theme! ?? "light";
const user = findUser("42")! ?? { name: "guest" };
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
declare const settings: { theme?: string };
declare function findUser(id: string): { name: string } | null;

const theme = settings.theme ?? "light";
const user = findUser("42") ?? { name: "guest" };
```

Here the `!` is what lets you read `label` before it is assigned, so it is allowed:

{/* good */}
```ts
let label: string;

const text = label! ?? "untitled";
```
